source.purpose: Validate product-level demand with net sales, net units sold by traffic source, sales channel, and new-versus-returning customer evidence rather than traffic or virality alone.
source.cost_quota: free public documentation; no paid credit used
source.requirements: Product Insights is viewed from Shopify admin product details and covers the last 90 days; Shopify says it is not currently available in the Shopify app.
source.reliability_limits: Documentation proves metric definitions and availability, not this store's current values or product demand. Store-specific data requires authorized admin read-back.

learning.title: Product traffic is not demand until it produces net units and net sales
learning.finding: Shopify Product Insights reports the last 90 days of net sales, net sales by channel, net units sold by traffic source, and first-time versus returning customers. Net units sold by traffic source can be negative when returns exceed sold units.
learning.old_approach: Traffic, virality, or gross unit movement could be overweighted when validating a product opportunity.
learning.new_rule: PRODUCT_SALES_SOURCE_GATE: do not treat traffic volume or virality as product demand by itself. When authorized Product Insights exists, cross-check traffic source against net units sold, net sales, sales channel, and new-versus-returning customer mix. Negative net units is an explicit return-risk signal, not positive demand.
learning.hypothesis_status: verified reusable measurement rule; store-specific values remain unknown until authorized read-back
learning.test_metric: For each candidate product with authorized data, record 90-day net sales, net units sold by traffic source, net sales by channel, and new/returning customer mix; compare like-for-like products and do not infer causality from traffic alone.
learning.fallback: If authorized Product Insights is unavailable, keep source-level net-sales contribution unknown and fall back to verified orders/sales/returns, landed cost, shipping, margin, trust, policy and seasonality evidence; never substitute virality.
